Applied.description:
What berth recorded on a host when it applied the configuration: its own
version and the plugins whose features the host has.

AppliedPlugin.description: A plugin as it was when a host's configuration was applied.

digest.description: SHA-256 of its files, so a change without a new version shows too.

choices.description: A command whose lines are the values to offer.

help.description: What it is for, in a sentence or two, beside its short label.

kind.description:
`resource` for an argument of a provisioner that sizes the machine:
its CPUs, memory or disk. `text` for one whose value has several
lines. Empty for any other argument.

secret.description:
What is given is a secret, such as a password: it is not shown as it
is typed, nor kept, nor written to a job's output.

values.description:
The values a provisioner's argument takes, when it is a choice of a
few. Empty for one that takes any text.

CommandLine.description: A list of arguments, or one string for `sh -c`.

agent_env.description: A wrapper that gives the agent its environment.

roots.description: Folders the file calls may touch.

systemd.description:
Whether the calls that need systemd work. Off in single-user mode
unless set.

units.description: Units whose state the stats report.

From.description: Who did something, as berthd saw it.

HostLevel.description:
How much of berth a host has: what its profile means it to have, or
what it was seen to have. Each level can do what the ones before it can.

KeptProfile.description:
The profile a host keeps of itself, at `/etc/berth/profile.json`: the
profile as berth holds it, without the enrollment key and without its
`access`, how the berth that wrote it reaches the host. A berth that does
not have the host can take it over from this.

berth.description: The version of the berth that wrote it.

format.description:
The format of this document: 2, or 1 for one berth 0.4.1 wrote, whose
profile has the layout before `access`.

host.description: The name the host has in the berth that wrote it.

instance.description: The same in a document of format 1.

machine.description:
The record of the machine berth created for the host, as a resource,
when it did.

written.description: When it was written, in RFC 3339.

cursor.description: Give it back as `since` to go on from here.

next.description: Pass as `since` for the rest, when there is more.

first_offset.description: Where what is still kept begins, when the start was dropped.

lines.description: The same as text, when read by lines.

offset.description: The offset this answer starts at.

cpu_time.description: Seconds of CPU used so far.

PublishFrame.description: What a client sends over the channel stream to publish.

lost.description: It ended with berthd or the host, not by itself.

task.description: The task it was started for, if any.

input.description: Text for standard input; a process then sees the end of its input.

timeout.description: Seconds after which the command is ended.

Started.description:
The answer to a start with `wait=`: the session and, when it has ended in
time, what it wrote.

cpu.description: Percent busy over 200 ms, all cores together.

extends.description: Tasks it is a step of; it then has no row of its own.

input.description: What the workstation sends on standard input: `secrets`.

oneOf.description:
What the host's configuration was last applied from, when berth
recorded it. An older berthd does not say.

What was installed on the host, by that record: `controller` when
only the controller was, `workstation` for a whole profile. Absent
when the host keeps no record.
